A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProPerSim and ProPerAssistant. All 31 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations across 32 personas, method comparisons in Table 1 and Figures 4–7, human quality assessments in Section 4.3, and a 353-participant rubric survey.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation, survey, and human-assessment results, and additionally reports intervention-success rates in Section 6.3.

M1.justification: Sections 3–5 retain the same simulation, structured memory, retrieval, preference-pair construction, and daily DPO procedure. The QLoRA-to-LoRA wording change in Section 6.2 revises the reported implementation setting without documenting different algorithmic steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same home-assistance task and 32 generated personas. Explicitly specifying all 32 personas in the human recommendation assessment clarifies previously unspecified coverage; it does not establish an expansion. Noisy or delayed feedback remains proposed future work.

E2.justification: Section 6.1 and Table 1 retain the same three comparators: No Memory, AR Memory, and ARS Memory. Their definitions and participation in the reported comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6.3 adds an intervention-success metric requiring an actual recommendation scoring at least 3, excluding 'No Recommendation'. Section 6.2 changes the stated fine-tuning method from QLoRA to LoRA while retaining the 4-bit LLaMA 3.3 70B model. These edits do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a diagnostic analysis of successful actual interventions over training, supplementing scores that also evaluate abstentions. The existing persona, personality-trait, evaluation-criterion, and qualitative case analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains the same SEM reporting. Neither version adds experimental run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests relative to the other; the new intervention rates are point estimates.

E6.justification: Section 4.3 changes the proportion of recommendation evaluations judged reasonable from 92.6% to 90.54%, without explaining the revision. Section 6.3 newly reports intervention success of 51.06% on Day 1 and 71.51% on Day 14. Table 1, plotted results, and appendix examples are unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definitions and Equations (1)–(4), along with Appendix A's distance and visualization mathematics, are unchanged. The added empirical success criterion introduces no accompanying theoretical derivation, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction now presents ProPerAssistant as a 'strong baseline instantiation', modestly reframing its contribution. The central claims about combining proactivity and personalization through ProPerSim and improving performance across 32 personas remain.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly acknowledges the focus on immediate rewards and identifies long-term satisfaction and noisy or delayed feedback as unaddressed extensions. Section 6.3 also removes the explicit efficiency comparison with computationally expensive reinforcement learning, while retaining the preference-learning interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-data repository footnote, explicitly documents that human recommendation assessment covers all 32 personas, and revises the fine-tuning reference to LoRA. Hardware, runtime, costs, and the detailed appendix prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the Dettmers et al. QLoRA citation with Hu et al. on LoRA and removes the Lewis et al. RAG citation and reference. It also frames ProPerAssistant as a baseline instantiation; the broader related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: Localized edits revise the introduction, human-validation description, and results discussion; rename 'Adaptation Across Diverse Personas' to 'Training on Diverse Personas'; and add acknowledgments. The section order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The header changes from 'Preprint' to the ICLR 2026 publication statement. Added text and the repository footnote produce limited spacing and pagination shifts. All seven figures and twenty tables retain their displays and captions.

improvement.justification: The added intervention analysis strengthens evidence about useful proactive behavior, while the new limitations and code/data access information improve transparency. These gains are modest: the main comparisons and appendices remain unchanged, and the reasons for the revised human-validation percentage and QLoRA-to-LoRA description are unexplained.
